What slows education teams down

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

  • Admission enquiries leak between ads, calls and walk-ins

    Leads arrive from Meta and Google forms, the website, education fairs, walk-ins and WhatsApp, often after office hours. Counselors work from personal phones and spreadsheets, follow-ups slip in peak season, and nobody can say which campaign actually filled seats.

  • Parents get many messages and still miss the important ones

    Circulars, homework, fee notices and photos land in crowded class groups. A same-day absence or a delayed bus is easily lost, and the school cannot tell who has read a trip consent slip or a safety notice.

  • Teachers spend evenings on administration

    Substitution plans, attendance registers, report card remarks, PTM scheduling and repeated parent questions eat into teaching and preparation time, and the extra work falls unevenly across staff.

  • Fee follow-up strains relationships

    Chasing dues by phone is slow and awkward, reminders sometimes reach the wrong person or a class group, and installment, concession and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts.

  • Learners drift away before anyone notices

    Coaching students fall behind after a few weak tests and doubts that never get answered, and online learners stop after the first modules. By the time a mentor notices, the learner has disengaged or asked for a refund.

  • Children's data and advertising rules are tightening

    Under the DPDP Rules as notified, from May 2027 institutions need verifiable parental consent for anyone under eighteen and may not track, behaviorally monitor or target ads at children beyond narrow exemptions, while coaching, consumer and UGC rules already add duties on claims, refunds and grievances. Class groups and spreadsheets make these hard to meet.

One admissions pipeline from first enquiry to confirmed seat

Every enquiry, whether from an ad, the website, a fair, a walk-in or WhatsApp, lands in one CRM with its source, gets an instant acknowledgment and a named counselor, and moves through campus visit or demo, application, document check and fee payment without falling between teams. Answers come only from the approved prospectus and fee schedule, and the admissions head sees the funnel by program and campaign.

What changes

  • Faster first responses to enquiries, including evenings and weekends
  • Fewer families lost between enquiry, visit and application
  • Counselor time goes to conversations instead of data entry and chasing
  • Admissions spend judged by confirmed seats, not just leads
  1. 1

    Capture every enquiry with its source

    Meta and Google lead forms, website forms, fair QR codes and walk-in tablets feed one CRM record per family, de-duplicated by phone number, with campaign, program or grade, campus, WhatsApp opt-in, consent and notice version recorded at capture.

    MAMeta AdsGAGoogle AdsGTGoogle Tag ManagerZCZoho CRMnn8n
  2. 2

    Acknowledge and assign within minutes

    Families who opted in get an approved WhatsApp template that thanks them, shares the prospectus link and names the counselor, assigned by program, campus and language; others get email or a DLT-registered SMS. Leads with no counselor contact in the agreed time escalate to the admissions head.

    Answer from approved content only

    Questions on fees, transport, dates, eligibility and documents are answered from the prospectus, fee schedule and admissions calendar the institution approves, citing the source. Anything else, or anything the model is unsure about, goes to the counselor.

    ACAnthropic ClaudeQQdrantnn8n

    Book the visit, demo or counseling call

    Families pick a campus tour, open-day slot, demo class or counselor call from live calendars, receive reminders with directions and reschedule in one tap. The counselor records the outcome after every visit.

    Collect the application and documents

    A secure link pre-fills known details and lists the documents each program needs. Uploads are checked for completeness and readability, and missing items trigger polite reminders until the office verifies the file. Under RTE Section 14, a missing age proof never blocks an elementary school admission.

  6. 6

    Confirm the seat and report the funnel

    After the admissions office approves, the family receives the offer and fee link, the record moves into the ERP through its API or import, and a daily dashboard shows enquiries, visits, applications and confirmed seats by program, campus and campaign.

  7. People decide

    Counselors own every family conversation. The admissions head approves templates, answer content and routing before launch, and only the admissions office decides eligibility, concessions and offers. The automation never screens or ranks children or parents, and RTE entry-level seats follow the state's own process.

A clear delivery rhythm

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 1

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We walk the student and parent journey with admissions, academic, transport, accounts and support staff, map where enquiries, messages and approvals pile up, and review what the ERP, LMS and test platform can expose. We also review consent forms, the privacy notice, the WhatsApp groups in use and current advertising claims.

  2. 2

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design flows, templates, routing rules and data flows, including the sensitive-message script for ragging, harassment and distress and the parent consent flow for under-18 learners. Academic content, fee and refund terms and consent wording are written or approved by your team, not by us.

  3. 3

    2–4 weeks

    Build

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against a test environment with synthetic student data, set up the consent log, staff queues and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

  4. 4

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test with counselors, teachers, transport and accounts staff, run scripted cases such as an absent child whose parent did not know, a ragging report or a fee dispute, fix what fails, and launch in one campus, grade band, program or batch before any wider rollout.

  5. 5

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor failed messages, template quality, handoffs and model accuracy, review KPIs with your owners each month and before each admission season, and change content and rules only through an approved change process.

First pilot: Four-week admissions desk pilot

Start with one campus, grade band, program or center. Enquiries from your ads, website and walk-ins land in one CRM, get an approved acknowledgment and a named counselor, and families book tours or demos on WhatsApp while counselors keep every conversation. We compare first response time and enquiry-to-visit conversion with earlier weeks. Out of season, absence alerts make a good alternative start.

  • One campus, grade band, program or center on an approved WhatsApp number
  • Lead capture from Meta, Google, the website and walk-in QR codes into one CRM
  • Acknowledgment, tour or demo booking and reminder templates approved by Meta and your admissions head
  • Counselor assignment with escalation to the admissions head
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of first response time and enquiry-to-visit conversion

Know whether it is working

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

Enquiry first response time
Median time from a new admissions enquiry to the first meaningful reply by a counselor or approved automated message, split by staffed and unstaffed hours.
Enquiry-to-enrollment conversion
Share of enquiries in a season that become confirmed admissions or paid enrollments, by source, program and campus.
Media cost per confirmed admission
Media spend for a campaign divided by the confirmed admissions or enrollments attributed to it in the CRM, for the same season.
Unexplained absence notification time
Time from the attendance cutoff to the parent being notified of an absence without approved leave, plus the share of unresolved cases phoned by staff the same day.
